chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Clef Club closure: political pressure and the court challenge
summary: Downtown establishments wanted 24-hour business; attorney Robert Carr challenged the closure in court, arguing hotels allowed the same bottle service, and the club won with Don Pacheco's help.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh -- well then, you know the story. But it was a great institution, musical institution. I really miss it, because there are a lot of people that I haven't seen since then, even the musicians. We just hear about them. the only time I see them is when I'm able to get down to the union to some union meeting, which is nowhere, you know. So we failed to see why it was doing any great harm, publicly, you know. But we found out later the reasons, you know, that and it was a political thing, it was given so much static was (unintelligible). But it was just great.
Who was it? Or do you want to say.

Well, there were certain establishments downtown that wanted 24 hour service, as far as entertainment and all that stuff. When I say entertainment, I don't mean musical. I mean wanted the people to spend their
money at their bars, you know, or either upstairs. And Attorney Robert Carr, who was the president of the corporation, took it to court and challenged it, and we won the case.
I remember there was -- I think I remember there were petitions going around, weren't there? Because I can remember signing some petitions.

Yeah. And a funny thing about it, we went to court and challenged the thing, and Bob Carr says, "Well, right now we can go in any one of these major hotels downtown and we can check in with our suitcase and take our bottle up to our room. We can call up the bellhop and order service and get our setups and whatnot." And says, "this is after 1:30, 2:00 o'clock in the morning, and we've got the same type of license. This is all we're doing." So we won on that account, here with the case in (unintelligible). We had a smart attorney And us, Don Pacheco, he was (unintelligible).
